name: CA-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about 18 points on the partisan index
Incumbent DeSaulnier holds a large fundraising edge with no outside opposition spending
Challenger Frese shows no reported fundraising or visible campaign infrastructure
Prediction markets price the race at roughly 96 percent Democratic
model.rationale: The district's deep Democratic lean, DeSaulnier's incumbency and financial advantage, and Frese's lack of visible fundraising all point the same direction, and markets price the race at about 96 percent Democratic. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the winner is barely in question and only the margin's size is uncertain.
model.watch: Any sign of serious challenger fundraising, outside spending against DeSaulnier, or an incumbent scandal would be the first indication the margin could tighten.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 10th District leans heavily Democratic, with a partisan advantage of roughly 18 points. Mark DeSaulnier, the incumbent, is seeking another term and has raised about $700,000 with more than $460,000 on hand. His Republican challenger, Jeff Frese, shows no reported fundraising in available records, and no outside groups are spending against the incumbent. No public general-election polls cover the race, and no expert raters have ranked it.

Prediction markets put DeSaulnier's chances at about 96 percent. The combination of a deep-blue electorate, incumbency, and a large financial edge leaves the challenger with little visible path. The realistic uncertainty concerns the size of the winning margin rather than the winner, since the district's fundamentals point strongly toward the incumbent party.
